items.note: Gemeenteblad 2025, 539473 (published 11-12-2025 09:00; council meeting 13 Nov 2025; art. 13: in force the day after publication, levy date 1 Jan 2026). Tariff table read in full: zone A 2.70 for first 2 h then 5.00/h; zone B (Mineurplein, St. Catharinaplein, Korenmarkt, Pastoor Joorenplein) 2.10/h, day card 13.50; zone C 2.00/h, day card 9.00 (adjoins zone A, defined on a map). All as written. Zone A is bounded by named singels and streets, so 'inside the singels' is a fair paraphrase. Ordinance text is the official published version; amounts are the tax tariffs, not designated hours.

Same ordinance, tariff table checked: zone E (Plein XIII and De Kaai incl. harbour sides; coach bay same tariff) 1.50/h, day card 7.50; zone D (Boerhaaveplein next to Lievensberg hospital car park, Van Swietenlaan, Mathijssenstraat, Wierlaan) 1.10/h, day card 5.00; zone F (around Bravis hospital, bounded by A4, Mathijsenstraat, Sterrelaan, Rooseveltlaan) 12.00 per day only; zone G camper spaces on the Boulevard 10.00 per overnight stay. Art. 8 says hours/places are set by a college decision, consistent with the draft's caveat.

Same ordinance, art. 4 tariff table points 4a-4d, all numbers match: first resident permit (one or two plates) 71.40 / 60.60 / 62.40 / 53.40 in permit zones A-D; second or further permit 261.00 / 246.00 / 252.60 / 79.20; business permit 523.80 / 426.60 / 438.00 / 397.20; visitor permit 2.30 per day (1.30 in zone D). Note 'first permit' covers one or two plates, so the summary phrase 'first car' should read 'first permit'.

Same ordinance: subscription spaces zone C 2.70/day or 349.00/year, Monday to Sunday; zone D same prices, Monday to Friday. Service permits (general) 2.50/day, 43.00/month, 501.00/year (also 13.50/week; government 501, medical/ANBI 252, shared mobility 252). Art. 10: naheffing 82.00; wheel clamp fitting/removal 168.65 (276.75 if between 18:00 and 09:00); art. 11: no remission. All as written. Surcharge amount verified on the ordinance.

Memo 'Bijlage 3 Memo Verbetering parkeergarage de Parade', dated 6 Oct 2025 (7 pages, all read). It confirms: garage is part of building 'Blok 6'; under-occupancy ('onderbezetting', 'afname in de bezetting'), nuisance from unwanted persons, vacant retail units around the garage; Krabbegat Vastgoed named as co-owner ('mede-eigenaar'); cost split for the pedestrian entrance follows VvE shares. It does NOT say the municipality holds no majority in the VvE; that statement is in the 26 June 2025 answers (the source of the later item), not in this memo.
items.corrected_text: The council memo of 6 October 2025 says the De Parade garage is part of the building Blok 6 and suffers from falling occupancy, nuisance from unwanted persons and vacant shops around it. It names Krabbegat Vastgoed as co-owner and says its contribution to the pedestrian-entrance works would follow the owners' association (VvE) shares.

items.note: Same memo: De Parade 'is een van de parkeerlocaties voor bezoekers van de binnenstad'; 'de afgelopen jaren is er minder gebruikersverkeer en minder behoefte om op deze locatie te parkeren. Hierdoor is er ook minder sociale controle'; poor/unclear access cited; garage 'weinig gebruikt'. No occupancy figures anywhere in the memo. Date 6 Oct 2025 matches.

Same memo: car-entrance bend radii widened and queuing lane lengthened with clear signing; open stair to first floor; lockable entrance on Sint-Josephstraat; major maintenance incl. renovation of the 2nd parking-level floor. Table total 2,580,000; subsidy Impulsaanpak Winkelgebieden 1,000,000; municipal co-financing 1,240,000. 20% margin and a still-to-be-drawn-up cooperation agreement with co-owner Krabbegat Vastgoed are stated. Worded as a proposal, as the memo is.

Same memo: sustainability (e.g. a solar carport enabling extra charging points) is not in the cost estimate; it 'kan worden opgepakt binnen de bredere verduurzamingsopgave van de gemeentelijke vastgoedportefeuille', and an indicative price for it is to be added in the final proposal. 'Left to the wider sustainability programme' is a slightly firm paraphrase of 'can be taken up within', but the substance matches.

Answers of 26 June 2025 to written questions from Belang van Bergen op Zoom (U25-003388), 3 pages read. Confirmed: 24-hour security hired by the VvE in 2023, stopped January 2024 because of high monthly costs. Pedestrian-entrance doors close after Jumbo closes at 21:00 'en binnenkort zodra de sportschool opent om 23:00u' (23:00 closing is announced as coming soon, not already in effect); then access only for visitors with a parking ticket scanned outside via QR or licence plate. The draft's 'now' is as of June 2025 and the 23:00 closing was future. The page also states the municipality holds no majority in the multi-owner VvE, which the draft attributed to the other source.
items.corrected_text: In answers to council questions dated 26 June 2025 the executive said the De Parade garage is part of a building with several owners, under an owners' association (VvE) in which the municipality has no majority share. It said 24-hour security hired by the VvE in 2023 was stopped in January 2024 because of high monthly costs. According to the answers, the pedestrian-entrance doors close after the Jumbo supermarket closes at 21:00 and, as announced for soon, once the gym opens, at 23:00; the entrance is then accessible only to visitors with a parking ticket, who scan it outside via QR code or enter the licence plate.

items.note: Raadsmededeling RMD25-0015 (23 April 2025, 'gevoelenspeilend', i.e. a sounding of opinion) read in full. Four documents to be replaced as listed with the right names and adoption dates (Visie Verkeer en Parkeren 2012, Beleidsnota Parkeren 2013, Verkeersplan 2014, Nota Parkeernormering 2015) by a new Nota Mobiliteit (2025-2035) and Nota Parkeernormering, prepared with Royal HaskoningDHV. Direction: 'het slimmer organiseren van auto-parkeren in het gereguleerd gebied' with area-based policy, and a neighbourhood approach based on the results of the parking survey (parkeeronderzoek). Note the memo implies a parking survey exists, but no results are in it.

Same RMD25-0015, p.6: the college foresees that 'voor het binnenstadsbezoek vormen de parkeergarage Parade en een mogelijke nieuwe vorm van parkeren op het Mineurplein de basis'; Mineurplein is designated in the Visie Binnenstad as an important parking location; and 'het verbeteren van de parkeercapaciteit wordt in samenhang opgepakt met de woningbouwopgave'. The draft's 'more parking capacity' overstates 'improving parking capacity'. Consultation text with no financial consequences, not a decision (as the draft says).
items.corrected_text: In a council communication of 23 April 2025 (a consultation text, not a decision) the executive said that for city-centre visits the De Parade garage and a possible new form of parking at Mineurplein should form the basis. It noted that Mineurplein is designated in the Visie Binnenstad as an important parking location, and that improving parking capacity would be taken up together with the housing programme.

items.note: The cited PDF (Motie Parkeernormen Wijkgericht) is a one-page motion on RVB25-0078 Nota Parkeernormen for the meeting of 18 December 2025 (scan text layer reads '1B'; the sister motion confirms 18 December). It asks to specify area typologies at district level and re-submit the Nota in Q2 2026. It says nothing about RVB25-0077, the first amendment, or disabled-card holders. I separately opened the sister motion (https://bergenopzoom.debatrijk.nl/documents/46/6288/documents/80573/Motie%20Toegankelijk%20en%20betaalbaar%20parkeren%20voor%20mensen%20met%20een%20beperking.pdf): on RVB25-0077 Bergse nota Mobiliteit 2025-2035 and the first amendment to the 2026 parking-tax ordinance, it asks the executive to investigate abolishing or compensating paid parking for minima (low-income) holders of a disabled-parking card on regular spaces (they have paid since 2021), and to report back in Q3. 'Debated' is not shown; only that motions were tabled. Vote results not read.
items.corrected_text: Two motions were tabled for the council meeting of 18 December 2025. One, on proposal RVB25-0078 Nota Parkeernormen, asked the executive to specify the area types in the parking-norms nota at district level and to resubmit the nota to the council in Q2 2026. The other, on proposal RVB25-0077 (Bergse nota Mobiliteit 2025-2035) and the first amendment to the 2026 parking-tax ordinance, asked the executive to investigate abolishing or compensating paid parking on regular spaces for low-income holders of a disabled-parking card (who have paid since 2021). The vote outcomes were not read.
items.corrected_title: Motie Parkeernormen Wijkgericht and Motie Toegankelijk en betaalbaar parkeren voor mensen met een beperking (18 December 2025)

items.note: Concept 'Toekomstbeeld Binnenstad Bergen op Zoom', 7 December 2022, by Urhahn for the municipality and Province of Noord-Brabant (colophon), marked CONCEPT. Text: two garages and a number of parking squares give sufficient visitor parking; aim to reduce cars on squares; ideally all visitors park in the garages and as little as possible on street; garages upgraded to parking hubs with (electric) shared cars; a new parking hub on the north side of the ring with the Mineurplein area on the singel as search area. All match. Old concept version (the October 2025 memo refers to the vision as 2023), hosted on the website of the entrepreneurs' association Sterck.

Same concept: 'Bij bezoekers van de binnenstad zijn de twee parkeergarages momenteel minder geliefd dan de parkeerpleinen'; better use via findability (garage Grote Markt) and accessibility (garage De Parade); inner-city residents park on the street, on a square, in the Grote Markt garage, or outside the centre (Plein13 or De Kaai). 'Currently' means December 2022.

News-item PDF (file name 2026-04-02; PDF creation date 1 April 2026) read in full. Page says: at the council meeting of 10 March 2026 the council also discussed the necessary investments in De Parade; priorities safety of construction and routing, usability incl. better flow at entrances/exits, and general appearance; 'heeft de gemeenteraad financiering beschikbaar gesteld'; works planned for 2027. No amount, no decision number. The host sterck.bergenopzoom.nu is the website of Ondernemersvereniging Sterck, the city-centre entrepreneurs' association (confirmed on its home page), so this is a business-association newsletter, not a council or municipal document; the draft could not identify the owner. My search found no council record of the 10 March 2026 decision. Medium confidence stands; single secondary source.
items.corrected_text: A news item of April 2026 (PDF dated 1-2 April 2026) from the website of Sterck, the city-centre entrepreneurs' association (not a council document), reports that at its meeting of 10 March 2026 the council discussed the necessary investments in the De Parade garage and made financing available, with the works planned for 2027. The council's stated priorities are safe construction and routing, better flow at the entrances and exits, and a more attractive appearance. The item gives no amount and no council decision was read.

items.note: Decision LG14072026, decision date 16-7-2026 (repository PDF, 15 pages, read). Confirmed: two spaces at each of four locations (Rondsel 1 Halsteren; Stelleweg 38; Zilverschoonplein 37; Duvenee 5) and one space at each of three (Beemdkroon 32a; Wittoucksingel 73; Ericalaan 61) = seven locations in Bergen op Zoom and Halsteren; the municipality uses kWh and number of charging sessions of existing posts and structural usage patterns; it has an agreement with a market party for public charging services. NOT on the page: that the locations are 'residential streets' or 'not the centre' (only street addresses and annex maps are given; I cannot confirm the location relative to the centre).
items.corrected_text: A traffic decision dated 16 July 2026 (LG14072026) designates one or two public charging spaces at each of seven locations in Bergen op Zoom and Halsteren: Rondsel 1 (Halsteren), Stelleweg 38, Zilverschoonplein 37, Duvenee 5 (two spaces each), and Beemdkroon 32a, Wittoucksingel 73 and Ericalaan 61 (one space each). It says the municipality uses monthly kWh and charging-session data of existing posts to decide where to expand, and that it has an agreement with a market party for public charging services.

items.note: Gemeenteblad 2026, 306191, published 26 June 2026, decision LG24062026 (2 pages read). Designates four parking spaces (Augustalaan 218, Prins Bernhardlaan 16, Noordsingel 152, Ansjovislaan 130) exclusively for Greenwheels shared cars during a three-year pilot; recitals cite the Bergse Nota Mobiliteit 2025-2035; site choice from CBS statistics (demographics per neighbourhood, car ownership per household, public-transport proximity, address density) plus use of existing Greenwheels cars and requests from residents. Draft wording matches. The decision enters into force one day after publication.

CVDR672709/1 read: 'Besluit tot aanwijzing plaatsen betaald parkeren ... 2022', in force 1 Feb 2022, registry says 'Geldend van 12-02-2022 t/m heden' (read 21 Oct 2026). Hours match: zone A Mon-Sat 09:00-21:00 with 2-hour maximum (1 hour at some spots); zone B Mon-Sat 09:00-21:00; zone C Mon-Sat 09:00-18:30, koopavond to 21:00 (Friday fixed koopavond), listing Parallelweg (between Wouwsestraatweg and Eikstraat) and Stationplein; zone E (De Kaai, Plein XIII etc.) Mon-Sat 09:00-18:30 with koopavond; zones D and F (hospital streets) Mon-Fri 08:00-19:00. A search of the CVDR open-data registry (SRU) for Bergen op Zoom parking regulations returned only the 2003 verordening, the 2017 and the 2022 decisions, so no newer designation in that registry; Gemeenteblad could not be searched exhaustively. Caveats: decision is four years old, zone letters/maps were drawn under earlier ordinances (hospital streets are now split differently in zones D/F of the 2026 ordinance), and a 2-hour cap sits oddly with the 2026 zone-A tariff, so current hours/limits are unverified. Keep confidence medium.

corrected_summary: Bergen op Zoom (Noord-Brabant) charges for street parking in its historic centre under the Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026, adopted by the council on 13 November 2025, published on 11 December 2025 and effective for the levy from 1 January 2026: in the core (zone A) 2.70 euros for the first two hours then 5.00 euros per hour, 2.10 euros per hour on the main squares (zone B) and 2.00 euros per hour in the surrounding ring (zone C), with lower rates near the hospitals, Plein XIII and the harbour. A first resident permit (one or two plates) costs between 53.40 and 71.40 euros a year depending on the permit zone, and the parking-fine surcharge is 82.00 euros. The paid-parking hours come from a 2022 designation decision (Monday to Saturday 9:00 to 21:00 in the core and squares, 9:00 to 18:30 in the ring and Plein XIII, with Friday evening to 21:00), which is still listed as valid in the national registry but may be out of date. A 2022 concept city-centre vision says the two centre garages (De Parade and Grote Markt) are less popular with visitors than the parking squares, and an October 2025 council memo says De Parade suffers from falling occupancy, nuisance and nearby shop vacancies; it proposes a refurbishment costed at 2.58 million euros, including 1.0 million euros of national subsidy. A news item by the city-centre entrepreneurs' association (not a council document) says the council made funding available for De Parade in March 2026 with works planned for 2027, but no amount or council decision was read. Policy documents point to a new Nota Mobiliteit 2025-2035 and parking norms, a possible parking hub near Mineurplein, and shared-car (four Greenwheels spaces, June 2026) and charging-point (seven locations, July 2026) roll-outs. No official source on the station park-and-ride, on garage operators or on measured occupancy could be read, so the picture of actual utilisation is thin.
